generatedCommentsNodes.comment:
The change removes the `refreshFailure` mechanism and instead collapses a refresh failure into `refreshed.set(false)`, so `maybeFinish` always calls `respond.onSuccess(refreshed.get())`. Two concerns:
1. **Silent exception swallowing.** In the `onFailure` handler (diff #BMM83), the exception `e` is received but never logged or otherwise recorded before being discarded. Previously it was propagated to the caller via `respond.onFailure(e)`. At minimum, the exception should be logged (e.g., `logger.warn("refresh failed", e)`) so that operators can diagnose why a refresh did not occur. Without any trace, a persistent refresh failure becomes invisible.
2. **Loss of failure signal to the caller.** The `onSuccess(boolean forcedRefresh)` contract (per its Javadoc) means "post-write actions completed; `forcedRefresh` is true iff a refresh was caused." After this change, a *failed* refresh is indistinguishable from a *skipped* refresh—both yield `onSuccess(false)`. If any downstream logic (e.g., a client waiting for a `refresh=true` write to be visible) relies on the failure path to retry or alert, it will now silently proceed as if the refresh simply wasn't needed. If this is intentional (e.g., the shard is now failed elsewhere as the removed TODO hinted), consider adding a brief comment at the `refreshed.set(false)` site explaining why the failure is safe to absorb here.

review_comment:
I am not entirely sure this is correct. The flag we are setting ends up in `forcedRefresh` I think. That flag is not an indication of whether the refresh succeeded. Rather it is whether the indexing operation forced a refresh for various reasons.

But in the timeout case, I suspect we could end up in having a response where the search shard is not necessarily refreshed?

Or are we failing the search shard also on a timeout failure? If so, that seems dangerous. But given that we apply the timeout [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/42dbc3d795c94ed3068dfd45d8b92e110c9076cc/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/support/replication/PostWriteRefresh.java#L149) I think that is not the case.

>But in the timeout case, I suspect we could end up in having a response where the search shard is not necessarily refreshed?

In the timeout case we [fail the bulk request](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/7f83189cb24bf41ddea13126385c47302ea9f9b3/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/support/replication/TransportWriteAction.java#L466-L471) too which seems wrong to me? 

> Or are we failing the search shard also on a timeout failure? If so, that seems dangerous. But given that we apply the timeout [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/42dbc3d795c94ed3068dfd45d8b92e110c9076cc/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/support/replication/PostWriteRefresh.java#L149) I think that is not the case.

No, we're not failing the shard after a refresh timeout.
